To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MyoD(-(-) satellite cells are defective in their ability to fuse with each other and to differentiate into myofibers.

the absence of MyoD leads to the following: 1) an elevated satellite cell population in adult muscle; 2) an abnormal branched fiber morphology; 3) a failure of MyoD(-)- satellite cells to upregulate MEF2 and MRF4; 4) a failure of satellite cells to fuse and differentiate; 5) an altered expression profile of genes involved in muscle development and regeneration.
MyoD-deficiency in satellite cells results in a differentiation-deficient phenotype, which may contribute to muscle wasting and regeneration defects in MyoD(-) animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the molecular mechanisms responsible for the observed MyoD-dependent defects in satellite cell differentiation, and the elucidation of the molecular and cellular mechanisms that regulate the balance between quiescence, activation, and differentiation in satellite cells.
the role of the MyoD family of basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors in the regulation of muscle cell differentiation and proliferation.
the role of the myogenic regulatory factors in the control of muscle cell fate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MyoD null mutation leads to a satellite cell differentiation deficiency that is not simply due to developmental arrest.
MyoD(-/ -) satellite cells are "differentiation defective" and that this phenotype is likely the major contributor to the observed disease phenotypes in MyoD-null mice.
the MyoD-deficiency phenotype is a complex and multifaceted one, and that the MyoR(-/-) muscle precursor cell has a distinct molecular and cellular identity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MyoD(-) satellite cells are defective in differentiation and that this is associated with a loss in MRF4 expression and an abnormality in m-cad gene expression.
MyoD(-/ -) satellite cells are defective in differentiation, but not proliferation.
MyoD is required in satellite cells for normal progression of the differentiation program.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MyoD is essential for normal satellite cell behavior and that its absence leads to a phenotype that is both unique and deleterious to the muscle fiber.
MyoD is essential for the maintenance of the satellite cell population and the normal progression of satellite cells through the cell cycle and the differentiation program.

loss of MyoD in adult muscle fibers has a major effect on the satellite cell compartment, which is not simply due to the loss of a transcription factor but rather reflects a complex interplay of gene expression changes that result in a cell that is unable to differentiate.
